Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion (al-Furqan) upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds, He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has not taken a son, and who has no partner in the dominion, and who created everything and determined it precisely.﴾

Tafsir of Surat al-Furqan

It is Meccan. Al-Dahhak said: it is Madani.

His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant﴾. Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr recited it as "upon His servants" in the plural. His saying: ﴿Tabaraka﴾ is a form (tafa'ul) derived from barakah (blessing). It has been said: tabaraka means: He is exalted by what has never ceased and will never cease. Al-Hasan said: Tabaraka is an attribute of Allah the Exalted, because every blessing comes from Him. Others said: it is because He is blessed by His name. As for barakah, it is goodness and increase. It has been said: the performance of every act of obedience by the servants is a barakah. Al-Buruk (the root) means firmness and steadiness, and it is said: so-and-so is blessed, meaning that goodness descends wherever he is.

His saying: ﴿who sent down the Criterion﴾, meaning: the Qur'an. The Qur'an was named al-Furqan (the Criterion) for two reasons: first, because it distinguishes between truth and falsehood; second, because it contains the explanation of what is lawful (halal) and unlawful (haram).

His exalted saying: ﴿upon His servant﴾, meaning: Muhammad (ﷺ).

His saying: ﴿that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾, meaning: the jinn and mankind. The scholars said: no prophet was sent to all the worlds except Noah and Muhammad, upon them be blessings and peace.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 2:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Him to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and who has not taken a son﴾, meaning: as the Christians say.

And His saying: ﴿And He has no partner in the dominion﴾, meaning: as the idol-worshippers and others say.

And His saying: ﴿And He created everything﴾, meaning: everything that is fit to be created.

His saying: (then He determined it with determination), meaning: He proportioned it with proportion, to suit the matter for which it was intended. It is also said: [He determined] the measures of things, their benefits, the measure of their duration, and the time of their passing away.

﴿And they have taken, besides Him, gods that create nothing, while they are themselves created, and they possess neither harm nor benefit for themselves, nor do they possess death, nor life, nor resurrection.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieve say: "This is nothing but a fabrication he has invented, and others have helped him with it." Indeed, they have brought injustice and falsehood. And they say: "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they have taken, besides Allah, gods﴾, means: the idols.

And His saying: ﴿who create nothing, while they are themselves created﴾, its meaning is apparent.

And His saying: ﴿and they control not for themselves any harm or benefit﴾, that is: repelling harm and bringing about benefit. This applies to the idols which the polytheists worshipped.

And His saying: ﴿and they control not death or life﴾, that is: causing death (and not giving life).

And His saying: ﴿nor resurrection﴾, that is: raising up after death.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "This is nothing but a lie he has invented, and others have helped him with it."﴾ That is: a falsehood he has fabricated.

And His saying: ﴿and others have helped him with it﴾ means: Jabr, Yasar, 'Addas, and Abu Fukayhah. These were slaves who were in Makkah from among the People of the Book, and they used to sit with the Prophet (ﷺ) and listen to him. So the polytheists claimed that Muhammad was taking from them.

And His saying: ﴿so they have produced injustice and falsehood﴾ means: with injustice and falsehood. When the preposition (bi, "with") was dropped, the word became accusative (manṣūb).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 5:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they say: "Tales of the ancients."﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: al-Nadr ibn al-Harith was among the devils (shayatin) of the polytheists. He had come to al-Hirah and had read the accounts of the kings of Persia. (He used to say to the polytheists: "Muhammad says [the Quran is] the tales of the ancients, but I will tell you the like of it," meaning from the stories of the Persians.) And [he related] the story of Rustam and Isfandiyar. So the verse was revealed concerning him and concerning whoever said his saying, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Umayyah al-Makhzumi and others.

﴿And asleep and awake... Say: "It was sent down by He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth. Indeed He is ever Forgiving and Merciful."﴾ And they say: ﴿"What is this messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets? Why was an angel not sent down to him so that he would be a warner along with him?"﴾

His saying: ﴿iktatabaha⁠﴾ means: he asked that it be written down for him, because he could not write.

His saying: ﴿fa-hiya tumla ʿalayhi⁠﴾ means: it is recited to him, since he could not write, so it is dictated to him that he may write it.

His saying: ﴿bukratan wa-asilan⁠﴾ means: in the morning and in the evening.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 25, verse 6:

﴿Say: "He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth has sent it down."﴾ That is: the unseen (al-ghayb) in the heavens and the earth. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ That is: Overlooking (of faults), Bountiful (in kindness).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 7:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "What is this messenger that eats food and walks in the markets?"﴾ They said this in the manner of denial, and they supposed that if he were like them, eating food and walking in the markets, then it would not be permissible for him to be singled out from them by prophethood. They used to say, "You are neither a king nor an angel. You are not a king, because you eat food, and you are not a king, because you go about the markets and humble yourself, whereas kings neither go about the markets nor humble themselves." All of this that they said is false. This is because his eating food does not contradict prophethood, nor does his walking in the markets. His eating food indicates that he is a human being in need, and his walking in the markets indicates that he is humble and not arrogant. As for his being singled out from among people with the excellence of prophethood, this is permissible, because Almighty God did not make people equal; rather, He gave some of them preference over others.

And His saying: ﴿"Why has an angel not been sent down to him?"﴾ They said this because they supposed that if the messenger were not a king, then he should have a companion among the angels. This too is false, because it is mere arbitrary judgment. It is possible for a human being to be singled out for prophethood without an angel being with him. Moreover, for the prophet to be a human being is better than for him to be an angel, so that they might understand from him and be at ease with him.

And His saying: ﴿"or be given a treasure, or have a garden from which he eats?"﴾ Its meaning: a partner.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 8:

And His saying: ﴿Or a treasure be thrown down to him﴾, meaning: a treasure be sent down to him from the sky, or a treasure appear for him in the earth.

And His saying: ﴿Or he have a garden from which he may eat﴾. They said: Why did God not make for you a garden by which you would live, or a treasure that He would give you, so that you would be independent of livelihood, earning, and exposing yourself to the affairs of the world? This too is invalid, because his earning and livelihood were not incompatible with his prophethood.

And His saying: ﴿And the wrongdoers say: You follow only a man affected by sorcery﴾. That is: deceived. It was also said: turned away from the truth. And it was said: one who is made to need food and drink.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿See how they coin comparisons for you﴾, meaning: they fashioned likenesses for you. The likenesses they cited were their saying that he is deluded, their saying that he is needy and abandoned in this world, and their saying that he is deficient in managing affairs and in attending to his own matter.

His saying: ﴿So they have gone astray﴾, meaning: they erred. It is also said: they contradicted themselves, for they would at one time say: he is a fabricator, that is, he uttered it of his own accord, and at another time they would say: he was taught it by someone else.

His saying: ﴿so they cannot find a way﴾, meaning: a path to the truth. It is also said: a path to obedience to God.

Glorified is He who, if He wills, will grant you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will grant you palaces.

Tafsir al-Quran of al-Sam'ani, on surah 25, verse 10:

The statement of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Glorified is He who, if He wills, will grant you better than that﴾ means: better than what they asked for you.

His statement: ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ means: orchards through whose trees' bases rivers flow.

His statement: ﴿and He will grant you palaces﴾ means: lofty houses, and the Arabs call every built-up house a qasr (palace).

Habib ibn Abi Thabit narrated from Khaythama that Allah the Exalted presented the keys to the treasuries of the earth to Muhammad (ﷺ), but he did not choose them. In some reports: "He was offered gold on the plain of Makkah, but I chose to be a servant-prophet."

Allah's words: ﴿Nay, they denied the Hour﴾ — i.e., the Resurrection.

And His words: ﴿And We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blazing fire﴾ — i.e., a fire ablaze; "mustaʿirah" means kindled, blazing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 12:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place﴾, and the rest of the verse. He narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever attributes to me what I did not say, on the Day of Resurrection he will be between the two eyes of Hell." It was said to him: "Does Hell have two eyes?" He said: "Yes," and he recited the Exalted's saying: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place﴾.

Some of them said: "When it sees them" means: its guardians (zabaniyya, the angels set over Hell) see them.

As for His saying: ﴿they hear its raging and roaring﴾. If it is asked: "How can one hear rage? Rage is only known." The answer to this: we say its meaning is: they hear the seething of rage. And before it: "they hear from it a roaring (zafir)," that is: they perceive from it rage. The poet said:

"I saw your husband in the battle, girding a sword and a spear,"

that is: girding a sword and carrying a spear. And another said:

"I fed her chaff and cool water,"

that is: I fed her chaff and gave her cool water. We have already mentioned the meaning of zafir (the roaring exhalation of Hell). It is narrated from Ubayd ibn Umayr that he said: "Hell will exhale one exhalation on the Day of Resurrection, and no angel or sent prophet will remain except that he falls on his face, until Abraham gets down on his knees and says: 'Myself, myself, and I want nothing else.'"

As for His saying: ﴿from a distant place﴾, it was said in some tafsir works: from a distance of one hundred years.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 13:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when they are cast into it, into a narrow place, bound together﴾. It is said: "tadayyaqa al-zajj fi al-rumh" (the butt-end of the spear became narrow in the spear).

And His saying: ﴿bound together﴾, meaning: shackled. It is also said: fettered, as if their hands were chained up to their necks, and they were bound together with the devils. We have already explained that every disbeliever is bound together with a devil in a chain.

And His saying: ﴿There they will cry out for destruction﴾, meaning: ruin, which is their saying: "Wa-ahlakah!" (Woe, our destruction!). And in some reports it is related that the first to be clothed in a garment of fire is Iblis, who will drag it to Hell, and his offspring will follow him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 14:

And His saying: ﴿Do not call out for one destruction today, but call out for many destructions.﴾ That is: this is not a place for calling for a single destruction, but a place for many calls. The poet said:

(When he follows Satan along the paths of error... and whoever Satan inclines toward is destroyed (mathbur).)

Mathbur means: ruined, lost.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 15:

His saying: ﴿Say: Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity which has been promised to the righteous?﴾ If it is said: there is no good at all in Jahannam (Hellfire), so how does His saying ﴿Is that better, or the Garden of Eternity?﴾ hold together?

The answer to this: We say: the Arabs sometimes mention the like of this even when neither of the two has any good at all. It is said: "Returning to the truth is better than persisting in falsehood." Al-Azhari said: The word "good" (khayr) is mentioned here only because the two abodes are equal in being places where people dwell, in the sense that they are two dwelling-places in which creatures are lodged, so it is correct to say: "This dwelling is better than that dwelling," because they share a common attribute.

And His saying: ﴿It shall be for them a recompense and a destination﴾ means: a requital (mujazah) and a place of return (marji'an).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish, abiding eternally﴾, i.e., remaining (muqimin).

And His saying: ﴿It is ever upon your Lord a promise [that is] sought﴾, i.e., requested (matluban). It is the request of the believers in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, and grant us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾, i.e., through the tongues of Your messengers. It is also said: the request is from the angels on behalf of the believers, and that is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, and admit them to gardens of perpetual residence which You have promised them﴾ — the verse.

And the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And [mention] the Day He gathers them and what they worship besides Allah﴾, meaning: the angels. It was said: Jesus and 'Uzayr (peace be upon them both).

And His saying: ﴿Then He will say﴾, meaning: Allah says: ﴿Did you mislead these, My servants, or did they themselves stray from the way?﴾, meaning: they went astray from the path.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 18:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿They will say: Glory be to You! It was not for us to take any protectors besides You﴾. That is: it was not for us to command them to worship us while we worship You. It is also said: whoever takes an enemy of another as a protector has taken someone other than Him as a protector.

His words: ﴿But You gave them and their fathers enjoyment﴾. That is: through abundance of wealth and children. It is also said: through long life. And it is said: through attaining what they desired.

His words: ﴿until they forgot the Reminder﴾. That is: they forgot Your remembrance and became heedless of You. It is also said: they abandoned the truth that You sent down. His words: ﴿and they were a people doomed (qawman bura)﴾. That is: destroyed. It is said: a man is ba'ir (ruined), meaning lost; a commodity is ba'ira, meaning unsalable. And it is related in a report that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek refuge from the ruin of the [unmarried women] (al-ayyim).

The poet, who was Ibn al-Zib'ara, said:

(O Messenger of the King, indeed my tongue is a mender of what I have torn, since I have become ruined (bur))

That is: lost.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 19:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then they have denied you in what you say﴾. This is addressed to the polytheists, for they used to claim that the angels, Jesus and Uzayr (Ezra) had called them to worship them.

And His saying: ﴿So you cannot avert [the punishment] nor find help﴾. That is, to avert the punishment from themselves. It was also said: [it means] to avert it from you (from the truth).

And His saying: ﴿nor find help﴾. That is, they are not able to prevent the punishment from themselves.

And His saying: ﴿And whoever among you wrongs, We will make him taste a great punishment﴾. That is, a mighty one.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they surely ate food and walked in the markets.﴾ In the verse is a reply to their saying: "What is wrong with this Messenger, that he eats food and walks in the markets?" This is in the sense of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: I am not something novel among the messengers,﴾ and [I am not except] a messenger like the rest of the messengers. So if it is permissible for the rest of the messengers to be human beings, then it is permissible for me to be a human messenger.

And His saying: ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others.﴾ Concerning it there are two views. The first: the meaning of ﴿trial﴾ is for the poor man, who says: "Why was I not rich like him?" And the sound view is a trial for the sick man, who says: "Why was I not healthy?" And like the noble man is a trial for the lowly, who says: "Why was I not noble like him?"

The second view: the verse was revealed concerning the chiefs of the polytheists together with the poor among the believers, and the poor among the believers were such as ʿAmmar, Ibn Masʿud, Bilal, Suhayb, Khabbab, Salman and others. When the polytheist wanted to become Muslim, he would think to himself, saying: "This is a religion that these wretched people have preceded me to, so I will not become a follower of them," and he would refrain from Islam.

And His saying: ﴿Will you be patient?﴾ means: so be patient.

And in a report it is that the Prophet said: "Indeed, in patience upon what you dislike there is much good," and it is a long report.

It is also said that the meaning of the verse is: "Will you be patient, or will you not be patient?" And from some of them that he saw one of the wealthy men who passed by him in his procession; he stopped and recited His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others. Will you be patient?﴾ Then he said: "Yes, we will be patient, our Lord; yes, we will be patient, our Lord; yes, we will be patient, our Lord," three times. Some of them attributed this anecdote to al-Muzani with al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman al-Muradi. And concerning Dawud al-Ta'i, that ﴿...those who do not expect a meeting with Us say: "Why were the angels not sent down upon us, or why do we not see our Lord?" Indeed they have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed with great transgression.﴾ Humayd al-Tusi passed by him in his procession, while Dawud was in his worn-out garments, and he said to himself: "Do you seek a worldly thing that Humayd has preceded you to?"

And it is narrated that a man passed by al-Hasan al-Basri, who was in a fine appearance and great worldly dignity, and he asked: "Who is this?" It was said: "This is the retinue of al-Hajjaj." He said: "This is one who took the world by its right."

And His saying: ﴿And your Lord is ever Seeing﴾ means: Seeing of your deeds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 21:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And those who do not expect a meeting with Us say﴾, meaning: those who do not fear a meeting with Us. Al-Farra' said: "al-raja' (hope) with the meaning of al-khawf (fear) is a Tihami dialect (lughah tihamiyyah)." Among its instances is His words, exalted is He: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not expect dignity from Allah?﴾, meaning: you do not fear the greatness of Allah. The poet said:

(La tartajī ḥīna talāqā al-dhā'idhā ... asb'atan lāqat maʿan am wāḥidan)

Meaning: he does not fear.

And His words: ﴿Why were not the angels sent down to us, or [why] do we not see our Lord?﴾ its meaning: "Why were the angels not sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?"

And His words: ﴿They have become arrogant within themselves﴾, meaning: they have exalted themselves within themselves. Their arrogance is that they refused to believe, and they sought a sign that no nation before them had sought.

And His words: ﴿and have transgressed with great transgression﴾, meaning: they have exalted themselves with a great exaltation. Al-'utuw (transgression) is excess in wrongdoing to its utmost limit, and their transgression here is their request to see Allah in order that they might believe.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 22:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿On the Day they see the angels﴾. The Day of seeing the angels is the Day of Resurrection.

And His saying: ﴿No good tidings on that Day for the criminals﴾. He said this because the angels give good tidings to the believers on the Day of Resurrection, so the criminals seek some hope from them, and they [the angels] say: "No good tidings for you." This is what 'Atiyya said. Some of them said: the meaning of the verse is that there are no good tidings for the criminals at the time when good tidings are given to the believers.

And His saying: ﴿And they will say, "A forbidding ban"﴾, i.e., forbidden, prohibited. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Forbidden, prohibited is Paradise for whoever does not say, 'There is no god but Allah.'" The poet said:

(I yearned for the farthest palm tree, so I said to it: "Ḥajran ḥarām, is there no way to those [distant] dwellings?")

It is also said that the meaning of the verse is: entry into Paradise is forbidden for the disbelievers at the very time when it is granted to the believers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 25, verse 23:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds﴾. That is: We will intend (ʿamadnā) what they did of deeds.

And His words: ﴿and We will make it scattered dust﴾. ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: al-hibāʾ al-manthūr (scattered dust) is what is seen in a window (kūwa) when the rays of the sun fall into it. Others said: al-hibāʾ al-manthūr is what rises from the hooves of horses at the intensity of their running.

And it is narrated from Yaʿlā ibn ʿUbayd, who said: it is the ash. Some scholars distinguished between al-hibāʾ al-manthūr and al-hibāʾ al-munbath, saying: al-hibāʾ al-manthūr is what is seen in the window, and al-hibāʾ al-munbath is what the winds scatter from the hooves of horses.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will be better in their abode and finer in their resting-place﴾. If it is said: how can there be a resting-place (maqil) in the Garden and a resting-place in the Fire, when they are not places of sleep? The answer to this: al-Azhari said: the maqil is the place of rest, whether one sleeps or does not sleep. And it is transmitted from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud that he said: The Day of Resurrection will not reach its midpoint until the people of the Garden take their midday rest (yuqilu) in the Garden, and the people of the Fire in the Fire. So he mentioned the qaylula (midday rest) because midday is the time of the qaylula, and its meaning here is the descent (nuzul), that is, that each of the two groups descends to its dwellings. It has also been related that God, exalted is He, shortens the Day for the believers until it becomes for them as the time between one prayer and another.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 25:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And the day when the sky will be split open with clouds﴾. Qatadah said: "Upon the clouds." It is said: "So-and-so came with his mount," meaning: upon his mount.

Most scholars hold that the sky will be split open over a white cloud in which the angels will descend. It is also related that the lowest heaven will be split open, and there will descend from the creation within it more than the number of the jinn and mankind. Then the second heaven will be split open, and there will descend from the creation within it more than the creation of the lowest heaven and of the jinn and mankind. And so it will be with the third heaven, and the fourth, up to the seventh. Then the Cherubim (al-Karubiyyun) will descend, then the bearers of the Throne (hamalat al-'Arsh). We have already explained earlier the words: ﴿Do they await only that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds, and the angels?﴾

And His words: ﴿And the angels will be sent down with a descent﴾, meaning: and He will send down the angels with a descent.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 25, verse 26:

God the Exalted says: ﴿The sovereignty on that Day will be true, belonging to the All-Merciful﴾. Its meaning: the true sovereignty on that Day belongs to the All-Merciful.

﴿And it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers﴾. That is: severe. And among its severity is that God lengthens that day for them, just as He shortens it for the believers, as we have explained.

In some reports it is related that Hell will boil (tafur) on the Day of Resurrection, so the people will scatter and disperse. Whenever they reach one of the regions, they find seven rows of angels who have joined their wings to one another, and then he recited: ﴿And it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers﴾.

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 25, verse 27:

And His saying: ﴿And the day when the wrongdoer will bite his hands﴾. The wrongdoer (al-zalim) here is ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt, according to the consensus of the people of tafsir (ijma' ahl al-tafsir, the scholarly agreement on interpretation). The occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of the verse is: "ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt had intended to embrace Islam. It is related that he prepared a feast and invited the Prophet (ﷺ). He said: 'I will not eat until you testify that there is no god but Allah.' So ʿUqba bore witness. ʿUqba was a close friend of Umayya ibn Khalaf, and he said to him: [...]." Al-Naqqash related this account, and concerning it this verse was revealed.

And His saying: ﴿The wrongdoer will bite his hands﴾, meaning: he will gnaw his hands out of regret. In some tafsir works it is stated that he will gnaw his hands until he reaches his elbows, then they will regrow, then he will gnaw them again, and so on repeatedly.

As for His saying: ﴿Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger﴾, meaning: I had taken his path.

Wa qawluhu: ﴿Ya waylata, laytani lam attakhidh fulanan khalilan﴾. Ay: Umayyah ibn Khalaf, wa qila: al-Shaytan, wa al-awwal huwa al-ma'ruf.

Translation:

And His saying: ﴿Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend!﴾ That is: Umayyah ibn Khalaf. It was also said: Satan. The first is the well-known view.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 29:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, he led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me﴾. That is: he led me away from the guidance after it had come to me. It was also said: "from the Qur'an."

And His words: ﴿And Satan is ever to man a deserter﴾. That is: abandoning (taraka).

It is well known in the accounts of the military expeditions (maghazi) that 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'it was taken prisoner on the Day of Badr, and the Prophet (ﷺ) had him killed in cold blood (sabran). He said: "Shall I be killed from among these, O Muhammad?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Who will look after the children?" He said: "The Fire." 

They differed concerning his killer. Some of them said: 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) undertook his killing. Others said: 'Asim ibn Abi al-Aflah protected the hornets' nest (hama al-dabr). Only 'Uqbah and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith were killed among the captives on the Day of Badr.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 30:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And the Messenger says, "My Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned."﴾ That is: abandoned, left aside. It is also said: they treated it as "hujr," i.e., nonsense (hadhayan).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 31:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We have made﴾. This verse was revealed as consolation for the Prophet and as a naming of him.

And His saying: ﴿for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals﴾, meaning: enemies from among the criminals. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, in one narration, that it refers specifically to Abu Jahl, who is Abu al-Hakam 'Amr ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughira, may the curse of Allah be upon him.

And His saying: ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as guide and helper﴾, its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 32:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ That is: just as the Torah and the Gospel were sent down to Musa (Moses) and Isa (Jesus).

And His saying: ﴿Thus, that We may strengthen your heart thereby﴾ That is: We sent it down in installments, just as We sent it down so that We might strengthen your heart thereby, meaning, that We might fortify your heart with it. It has also been said: so that your heart might grow in insight, as if whenever Jibril (Gabriel) brought the revelation, he increased in insight and strength. Allah Exalted sent down the Qur'an over twenty-three years, and when Allah Exalted had completed what He willed to send down to him of revelation, death overtook him.

And His saying: ﴿And We have arranged it in measured order﴾ That is: We made it distinct in detail. It has also been said: We explained it with clear explanation.

Reciting with tartil (measured, deliberate recitation) is a sunnah, and it is disliked to recite in the manner of the chanting of poetry (hada' al-shi'r) or the scattering of dry dates (nathr al-diql).

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And they do not come to you with any example⁠—﴾ meaning: they seek to repel what you have been sent with, "except that We have brought you the truth," meaning: We have brought you that which repels and nullifies it. So he called the objections they put forward "a similitude" (mathal), and called that which repels the objections "truth" (haqq), which He gave to him.

And His words: ﴿and better explanation⦅tafsir⦆﴾. Tafsir is a form of the verb from al-fasr (tafsir: "explanation"), and al-fasr means uncovering what has been covered.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 34:

Allah's statement: ﴿Those who will be gathered on their faces to Hell﴾. Concerning this, the reports state that people will be gathered in three categories: one category riding, one category walking, and one category upon their faces.

The report has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) through the narration of Shayban, from Qatadah, from Anas that it was said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "How will people be gathered upon their faces?" He said: "Indeed, the One who made them walk upon their feet is capable of making them walk upon their faces."

He (may Allah be pleased with him) said: This was related to us by al-Makki ibn Abd al-Razzaq, who said: my grandfather related to us, who said: al-Farabri related to us, who said: al-Bukhari related to us, who said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Musnadi related to us, from Yunus ibn Muhammad, from Shayban... the report.

As for His statement: ﴿They are worse in position﴾, meaning: worse in rank and station.

And His statement: ﴿And further astray in way﴾, meaning: further wrong in path.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 35:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, and We made his brother Aaron with him a minister﴾, meaning: a helper and an assistant.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So We said, "Go both of you to the people who denied Our signs."﴾ And they were the Copts (al-Qibt).

And His saying: ﴿Then We destroyed them with complete destruction.﴾ That is: We caused them to perish with a total annihilation.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 37:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the people of Noah, when they denied the messengers﴾. He means: the Messenger; "messengers" is a plural used in the sense of the singular. It is said: whoever denies one single messenger has denied all the messengers; therefore He said: ﴿they denied the messengers﴾.

And His saying: ﴿We drowned them and made them a sign for mankind﴾. The water descended from the sky for forty days, and gushed forth from the earth for forty days, until the whole world became a sea.

And His saying: (And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment), meaning: painful.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And ʿAd and Thamud﴾, meaning: We destroyed ʿAd and Thamud.

And His saying: ﴿and the companions of the Rass﴾. Most scholars hold that the Rass (a well) is a well. It is related that when their prophet came to them, they put him into the well and threw upon him what destroyed him.

Al-Kalbi said: God sent to them a prophet, and they cooked him and ate him.

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, in some narrations, that the companions of the Rass were the people of Habib al-Najjar, who threw him into the well until he perished, and it was at Antioch.

And His saying: ﴿and generations between those many﴾. We have already explained the meaning of qurun (generations/centuries) earlier. It is related from al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym that he fell ill, and it was said to him: "Shall we not call a physician for you?" He said: "Give me time." Then he reflected within himself, then said: God the Exalted said: ﴿And ʿAd and Thamud and the companions of the Rass and generations between those many﴾. There were among them the sick and the physicians, yet neither the one who treats nor the one who is treated remained. I do not want you to call a physician for me.

Allah's words: ﴿And to each We set forth parables﴾, i.e., examples (al-ashbah).

﴿And each We utterly destroyed with complete destruction﴾, i.e., We annihilated them with annihilation (tadmir). It is also said: We destroyed them with destruction (ihlak).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 40:

Allah's words: ﴿And they have certainly passed by the town upon which a rain of evil was rained down.﴾ It is said: they are the towns of Lut (Lot). And it is said: the stone would descend to the height of a human being, and fall upon him, crushing him and destroying him.

And His words: ﴿Have they not been seeing it?﴾ He mentioned this because the cities of Lut were on their route during their passage to al-Sham (Syria) and their return from it.

And His words: ﴿Rather, they did not expect a resurrection.﴾ That is, they did not fear a resurrection. It is also said: "yarjun" retains its literal meaning, that is, they did not hope for the return to Allah, the Exalted.

﴿When they see you, they take you not except in mockery﴾ — i.e., they do not take you except as a [subject of] ridicule.

And His saying: ﴿"Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"﴾ — they said this in the manner of mockery.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 42:

His words: ﴿Indeed, he nearly led us astray from our gods﴾, meaning: he had nearly led us astray from our gods.

The poet says:

(I resolved, but did not act; I nearly did, would that I had left the wives of ʿUthmān weeping over him)

His words: ﴿Had we not been steadfast in them﴾, meaning: had we not been steadfast in worshipping them, he would have led us astray from them.

His words: ﴿They will know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in path﴾, meaning: who erred further in path.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 43:

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god?﴾ The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: Among the ways in which they took their desires as their gods was that one of them would worship a stone, and when he saw a stone better than it, he would discard the first, take the second, and worship it.

As for His saying: ﴿Would you then be a guardian over him?﴾ That is: a protector (ḥāfiẓan), and it has been said: a guarantor (kafīlan).

In some reports: There is no object of worship in the heavens and the earth greater than desire (al-hawa). And from some of them it is related that he said: It is the greatest tyrant (al-ṭāghūt al-akbar).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 44:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do you think that most of them hear or understand?﴾. That is: "Do you think?"

And His saying: ﴿They are only like cattle﴾. That is: they are nothing but like cattle. He made them like cattle because they did not perceive the path of truth, and did not benefit from what Allah distinguished them with over the beasts: their intellects, their hearing and their sight.

And His saying: ﴿Rather, they are more astray in way﴾. That is: they are more mistaken in the path. He placed the disbelievers as more astray than cattle, because cattle prostrate and glorify Allah, may He be exalted, while the disbelievers do not prostrate nor glorify Him. Also, cattle did not know, and they had not been given the instrument of knowledge; but as for the disbelievers, they did not know although they had been given the instrument of knowledge, so they are more astray. And also, cattle have not corrupted the knowledge they possess, for Allah, may He be exalted, gave them a measure of knowledge and they use it; but as for the disbelievers, they have corrupted the knowledge they have, so they are more astray and lower than cattle.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 45:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shadow?﴾ Some of them said: This is by way of inversion (al-taqdim wa'l-ta'khir), and its meaning is: Have you not considered how your Lord extended the shadow? It was also said: It is on its apparent sense, and the meaning of seeing (al-ru'yah) is knowing (al-'ilm). The poet said:

(Show me a horse that died of emaciation, so that perhaps I may see what you see, or a miser who lives forever)

They differed concerning this shadow. The majority hold that it is the shadow from the time of the rising of dawn until the time of the rising of the sun. The second view is that it is from the time of the setting of the sun until the time of its rising. The shadow here is the shadow of the earth, which advances at the setting of the sun and recedes at its rising.

As for His saying: ﴿And had He willed, He would have made it still﴾, that is: constant.

And His saying: ﴿Then We made the sun over it an indicator﴾, that is: Then We made the sun an indicator of the shadow, for the shadow is known by the sun, light is known by darkness, and night by day, and likewise all things are known by their opposites.

It was also said: "We made the sun over it an indicator" means: it follows it and pursues it, and then it abrogates it (fa-yansakhuhu).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 46:

And His saying: ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, withdrawing it gradually﴾

Al-qabd (the act of gathering in, withdrawing) is the gathering of what has been spread out of a thing. Its meaning is that the shade covers the earth, like the rising of the sun. When the sun rises, the shade is gathered in by the sun part by part. Thus it is said: the time of the shade's withdrawal is at the zenith, until no shade remains in the world except in a place where the sun is not directly overhead.

And His saying: ﴿yasiran﴾ means: easily. Mujahid said: unnoticeably, and this is the more correct of the two opinions.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who made the night for you as a garment﴾, meaning: He covers you with the darkness of the night when it envelops you, so the night is as a garment for people. Some of them said: it has the same meaning as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is He who made the night for you that you may rest therein﴾, and the place of rest is like a garment for the human being.

And His saying: ﴿and sleep as rest (subatan)﴾, meaning: repose. Al-sabt (cutting off, rest) means severing, and the sleeper is masbut (one whose activity is cut off), because his activity has ceased while the spirit remains in him.

And His saying: ﴿and made the day for rising (nushuran)﴾, meaning: a time in which they disperse.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 48:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is He who sends the winds as glad tidings﴾. It is also read as "nushran" with a damma on the nun and the shin, and it is read with a damma on the ba' (as "nushran"). So his saying "nushran" with a fatha on the nun means: for the raising up (inshar) of plants, and the raising up of plants is their revival. As for "nushran" with a damma on the nun, it is the plural of "nashr," like "rusul" is the plural of "rasul." As for ﴿bushran﴾ with a ba', it is from al-bushara (glad tidings). We have already discussed the matter of the winds.

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that when the wind blew he would say: "O Allah, make it winds (riyah) and do not make it a single wind (rih)."

They said: It was mentioned in this form because glad tidings come from three kinds of winds: the eastern wind (al-saba), the northern wind (al-shamal), and the southern wind (al-janub). As for the western wind (al-dabur), there is no glad tiding in it, because it is the barren wind (al-'aqim). And it is narrated from Mujahid that he said: The wind has two wings and a tail. And it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: The wind and the water are the greatest army of Allah.

His saying: ﴿before His mercy﴾ means: the rain.

His saying: ﴿And We send down from the sky pure water﴾. Tha'lab said: The tahur (pure) is that which is pure in itself and purifies others. So water is tahur because it purifies people from ritual impurities (ahdath), and purifies the land from barrenness (judub) and drought (qahat).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 49:

And the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿That We may give life thereby to a dead land﴾, meaning: a dead land (balda maytan). Its giving life is by causing vegetation to grow and by bringing forth trees and fruits.

﴿And We give drink therefrom to many of the cattle and people that We have created﴾, meaning: We give water to drink to cattle and many people. Al-anasi (sing. insi, and it is also said: the plural of insan) is the plural; its original form was anasin, like bustan and basatin, then the nun was dropped and the yaa was doubled (shaddah).

The meaning of the verse: We give water to drink to living beings and non-living things alike, causing to grow thereby everything that is capable of growth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 50:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have certainly variously repeated it among them﴾. Most of the exegetes (ahl al-tafsir) hold that the pronoun refers to the rain, and the meaning of tasrif (variation, distribution) is that He waters one land and withholds from another land.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "No year is wetter than another year, but Allah distributes it among His servants as He wills." Similar is related from Ibn Mas'ud.

It is also narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no hour that passes but the clouds are raining during it, except that Allah, may He be exalted, turns it away from one people and gives it to another people." The report is gharib (weak or unusual in its transmission).

As for His saying: ﴿that they may take heed﴾, i.e., that they may remember (liyatadhakkaru). It is also said that the pronoun in His saying ﴿We have repeated it﴾ refers to the Furqan mentioned at the beginning of the surah, but this is a distant view (qawl ba'id).

As for His saying: ﴿But most of the people refuse except ingratitude﴾, i.e., ingratitude (kufran). Their ingratitude is that when they are given rain, they say: "We have been given rain by such-and-such a star (bi-nawʾ kadha)." This is in the same sense as His saying in Surat al-Waqi'a: ﴿And you make your provision that you deny [the truth]﴾. It has also been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said one day, when they had been given rain during that night: "Allah, may He be exalted, says: 'In the morning people have become two groups: a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the star, and a believer in the star and a disbeliever in Me. Whoever says: "We have been given rain by the mercy and bounty of Allah, may He be exalted," he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the star; and whoever says: "We have been given rain by such-and-such a star," he is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the star.'"
The saying of Allah, the Most High: ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised in every town a warner.﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

Qur'anic quotations: "So do not obey the disbelievers" and "and strive against them with it, a great striving."

And His saying: ﴿So do not obey the disbelievers﴾, meaning: in what they call you to.

And His saying: ﴿and strive against them with it, a great striving﴾, meaning: with the truth. It is said: with the Qur'an.

And His saying: ﴿great﴾ means: severe.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 53:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who let loose the two seas⁠—⁠﴾ means: He mixed the two seas. It is also said: He sent forth the two seas.

As for "the two seas," it is said that they are the sea of Persia and the sea of Rome. It is also said: they are the sea of the sky and the earth. It is also said: the two seas are the salty and the sweet.

His saying: ﴿This one is sweet and palatable⁠—⁠﴾ every sweet water is called furat (palatable, sweet), and every salt water is called bahr (sea).

His saying: ﴿and this one is salty and bitter⁠—⁠﴾ means: intensely salty. It is also said: bitter.

His saying: ﴿and He placed between them a barrier and an inviolable partition⁠—⁠﴾ It is said: [the barrier is] by dryness between the two seas. It is also said: by air between the sea of the sky and the sea of the earth. It is also said: by divine power between the salty and the sweet, so that the salty does not mix with the sweet, nor the sweet with the salty; and this is in a specific place, the gulf of Egypt. The barrier (barzakh) is the hindrance.

His saying: ﴿and an inviolable partition⁠—⁠﴾ means: a prevention, prevented. The poet said:

(Many a one with a curtain [well] guarded... I have travelled to him from the heights of the wall.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who created from water a human being and made him [a relation by] lineage and marriage.﴾

Nasab (lineage) is kinship by blood relation, and sihr (marriage relation) is association from outside of lineage. We have already mentioned that Allah, exalted is He, forbade seven [women] by nasab and seven by sabab (marriage or fosterage), and we enumerated them in the commentary on Surat al-Nisa'. It is also said: nasab is that which makes marriage forbidden, and sihr is that which does not make marriage forbidden.

As for His saying: ﴿And your Lord is ever Competent⁠—﴾ meaning: capable.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 55:

The words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿And they worship besides God that which neither benefits them nor harms them﴾. This has already been mentioned.

And His words: ﴿And the disbeliever is ever a helper (zahir) against his Lord﴾, meaning: a helper to Satan in acts of disobedience. It is also said: "zahiran" means "contemptible" (hayyin), as a man says: "You have made me a thing behind the back (bi-zahr)," meaning: you have made me contemptible. The poet said:

(Tamim ibn [Zayd], let not my need be a thing behind the back, so that it is not difficult for him to answer it.)
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good news and a warner﴾. That is: bringing good news and warning.

And His saying: (Say: I ask you no reward for it), meaning: no wage (ja'l, a stipulated reward).

And His saying: ﴿except for whoever wills to take a way to his Lord﴾. Its meaning: "But whoever wills to take a way to his Lord" follows the path of faith and holds fast to it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 58:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die﴾. "The Ever-Living who does not die" is Allah, may He be exalted.

And His saying: ﴿And glorify Him with His praise﴾, i.e., pray by His command.

And His saying: ﴿And sufficient is He as one who is Acquainted with the sins of His servants﴾, i.e., Allah is sufficient as One who knows the sins of His servants, and this is in the manner of a threat and warning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 59:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days﴾ — we have already explained this.

And His words: ﴿Then He istawa (rose) over the Throne, the Most Merciful﴾ — we have already explained this.

And His words: ﴿so ask about Him one well-informed﴾ — it is said that its meaning is: ask about Him one who is informed (khabir), i.e., knowing ('alim), and that is Allah, the Exalted.

The poet said: (Why did you not ask the horses, O daughter of Malik... if you are one who asks about what you do not know)

i.e., about what one does not know.

It is also said: ask with your asking directed to the One who is informed (al-khabir), meaning: ask Me and do not ask other than Me. It is also said: the address is to the Messenger, and what is meant by it is the community (ummah), for he was knowing of this and affirming of it.

The real meaning is: that you, O human being, do not turn to anyone other than Me in seeking knowledge of this, as said by al-Zajjaj.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 60:

And His the Exalted's saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate yourselves to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful?"﴾

The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: They only said this because they did not recognize the name al-Rahman (the Most Merciful) in their speech, so they asked about "al-Rahman" for this reason.

It is also narrated that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called them to "al-Rahman," and it is said that Abu Jahl said to him: "O Muhammad, who teaches you the Qur'an?" Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿The Most Merciful, who taught the Qur'an﴾. Abu Jahl and others said: "We do not know al-Rahman except Musaylimah in al-Yamamah," and he used to be called "Rahman of al-Yamamah."

And His saying: ﴿Shall we prostrate to what you command us?﴾ means: to the Most Merciful whom you command us to prostrate to.

And His saying: ﴿and it increased them in aversion﴾ means: distance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 61:

His words: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the heaven constellations (buruj)﴾. They are the great stars (al-nujum al-izam). It was also said: they are the twelve constellations (al-buruj al-ithna 'ashara).

His words: ﴿and placed therein a lamp (siraj)﴾, meaning the sun. It was also read as "sirajan" in the plural (sirajan, "lamps"). According to this reading, the moon is also included among the lamps, except that He singled it out for mention because of a particular virtue it has. This is like His words, exalted is He: ﴿therein are fruits, palm trees and pomegranates﴾.

His words: ﴿luminous (muniran)﴾, meaning shining.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 62:

His saying: ﴿And it is He who made the night and the day alternating﴾ (khilfah). There are two opinions regarding it. The first: "differing from one another; this one is black and this one is white." The second: "khilfah" means that each one succeeds the other, i.e., one of them replaces the other. It is said: whatever remembrance (dhikr) was missed during the night, the day replaces it in that regard, and whatever remembrance was missed during the day, the night replaces it in that regard. Qatadah said: "And likewise in prayer." The third opinion: "khilfah" means that what decreases from one increases in the other, and what decreases from the other increases in this one. The poet recited regarding khilfah:

(In it are the eyes and the wild cows walking in succession... and their young ones rising up from every resting place.)

Based on this, khilfah means each of them succeeds the other.

And His saying: ﴿for whoever wishes to remember﴾, i.e., to be mindful (yatadhakkar).

﴿or wishes gratitude﴾, i.e., thankfulness (shukran).

Its meaning: whoever wishes remembrance or gratitude, then the night and the day are the times of remembrance and gratitude.

The Words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful﴾. If someone says: "Are not all people the servants of the Most Merciful, both believers and disbelievers?" We say: This is like when a speaker says: "my son, so-and-so," singling out one from among his children by it; and similarly he says: "my friend, so-and-so," singling out one from among his friends by it. Its meaning is that whoever is to be my son ought to be like so-and-so, and whoever is to be my friend ought to be like so-and-so.

And His words: ﴿Who walk upon the earth in humility﴾. That is, with tranquillity and dignity. Al-Hasan said: "They are scholars and wise, not ignorant when ignorance is directed at them." Tha'lab said: "Hawnan" means gently.

And from some of them: humble, not arrogant.

And His words: ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace"﴾. Al-Dahhak said: "When they are harmed, they pardon." Some of them said: "They say a saying from which they are safe." And from some of them: "They say 'Salaman,' that is, a disengagement, neither good nor evil." The intended meaning of "salam" is not the well-known greeting; rather its meaning is what we have explained.

The verse is Meccan. The Muslims had been commanded before the Hijrah to pardon and turn away, and not to repay the harm of the polytheists with retaliation. Then it was abrogated when they emigrated, by the verse of the sword.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 64:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing.﴾ It is said: "Fulan spent the night" (bāta), whether he slept or did not sleep.

The poet said:

(So we spent the night standing beside the head of our steed, it grappling with us from its own self, and we grappling with it.)

His saying: ﴿prostrating and standing﴾.

That is: prostrating upon their faces, and standing upon their feet.

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: Whoever prays two rakʿahs or more after the night prayer (ʿishāʾ), then he is among those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 65:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, turn away from us the punishment of Hell"﴾, meaning: turn away from us the punishment of Hell.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, its punishment is ever clinging (gharaman)﴾.

That is: a constant, perpetual clinging (multazaman dā'iman). Abu 'Ubayda said: it means destruction (halākan). It is also said: "So-and-so is gharim (infatuated/addicted) with women," meaning he has no patience to refrain from them, and from this comes al-gharim (the creditor/debtor who is owed or owes), because he clings to (lāzama) the one he is owed by or owes. It was also said that gharaman means severe, and al-A'sha said:

(If He punishes, the punishment will be gharaman, and if He gives, it will be generous, and He does not care.)

And from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: God demanded from the disbelievers the price of the blessing; when they were unable to pay, He made the blessing a debt upon them, so they remained in the Fire.

And from al-Hasan, who said: Every creditor parts from his creditor except Hell, for it never parts from its creditors ever.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, it is evil as a place of settlement and residence﴾. That is, how wretched is the place of rest, and the place of residence is Hell (Jahannam). We have already explained the difference between maqam and maqam.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 67:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy﴾. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hilli said: Every expenditure in other than the obedience of God is extravagance (israf), and every withholding from the obedience of God is niggardliness (iqtar).

And from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, he said: ﴿Neither extravagant﴾, i.e., they did not exceed the limit in spending, and that is by excess in expenditure in the manner of squandering (tabdhir).

And His saying: ﴿nor niggardly﴾, i.e., they did not restrict in spending until they left [those for whom they are obligated to provide] naked or hungry, those whom it is obligatory upon them to support.

And some of them said: ﴿Neither extravagant﴾, i.e., they did not spend in what is not right, and ﴿nor niggardly﴾, i.e., they did not withhold what is right; and this statement is close to the first statement.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: "And that is between them, a balance (qawaman): a good deed between two bad deeds." And Tha'lab related that Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan said to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, who had married his daughter Fatimah to him: "How is your spending, O Umar?" He replied: "A good deed between two bad deeds."

And from Wahb ibn Munabbih, that he said: "If you take hold of one of the two ends of a stick, it tilts; but if you take hold of its middle, it balances."

And His saying: ﴿qawaman﴾, i.e., moderate (adlan), which is the meaning of what we have said. And qawam with a fatha (qawam) is from uprightness (istiqamah), while qiwam with a kasra (qiwam) is that by which a matter is maintained, as if it were its foundation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 68:

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ — its meaning is well known.

And His words: ﴿nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾. "The right" (al-haqq) is what has been established from the Prophet, that he said: "The blood of a Muslim man is not lawful except by one of three (things) ..." And we have explained it.

And His words: ﴿nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse﴾. Zina (unlawful sexual intercourse) is a well-known act. As for sodomy (liwat): is it zina or is it not zina? The matter concerning it is as known in jurisprudence (fiqh), and likewise bestiality (ityan al-bahima).

It has been established through the narration of Amr ibn Shurahbil, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, that he said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" He said: "That you set up a rival (nidd) to Allah while He created you." I said, "O Messenger of Allah, then which?" He said: "That you kill your child out of fear that he will eat with you." I said, "Then which, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "That you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbour." Then he recited His words: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾, to the end of the verse.

He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Abu al-Abbas al-Azhari informed us of this hadith; [Abu al-Husayn] Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Khaffaf informed us; Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj informed us; Ishaq al-Hanzali informed us; Jarir informed us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il, from Amr ibn Shurahbil... the report.

Al-Kalbi mentioned that Wahshi sent to the Prophet seeking repentance for himself, so he sent to him this verse. Wahshi said: "I have associated others with Allah, I have killed, and I have committed adultery, and I do not know how my repentance can be? So I want a verse broader than this one." Then Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾. So he sent the verse to Wahshi, and he said: "I do not know, am I included in the 'whom He wills' or not? I want a verse broader than this verse." Then Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾. So he sent the verse to him, and he embraced Islam.

﴿Except one who repents﴾.

The people of knowledge said: This is extremely improbable, because this verse is Meccan, and Wahshi embraced Islam only after the battle of Hunayn and al-Ta'if, at the end of the Prophet's time, and all these verses were revealed (before his Islam by a number of years).

And in some tafsir works: This verse was revealed in Mecca up to His words: ﴿except one who repents﴾, and the people remained two years, then after that the words of Exalted Allah were revealed: ﴿except one who repents﴾ to the end of the verse.

And from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, that His words ﴿except one who repents﴾ refer to shirk and zina. As for the killing of a soul, Allah, Exalted is He, has revealed concerning it: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally...﴾ the verse. Ibn Abbas said: This verse is Medinan, and His words ﴿except one who repents﴾ are Meccan; so the ruling on killing is according to this verse, and there is no repentance for one who kills a soul.

As for others among the people of knowledge: repentance from all of them is accepted, and we have explained this before, and the apparent meaning of this verse, namely His words ﴿except one who repents﴾, indicates this, because the killing of a soul has already been mentioned.

And His words: ﴿And whoever does that will meet a penalty (athaman)﴾, i.e., the recompense of sin. It is said: "athaman" is a valley in Hell. The poet said:

"May Allah recompense Ibn Urwa, since he has become one who disobeys (his parents) ... and disobedience for him is a penalty (athaam)"

i.e., the recompense of sin. Another said:

"I have met destructions in our war ... and after destructions you will meet a penalty (athaman)"

The saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿His punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning: the punishment will be made to continue for him. It is also said: Allah doubles the punishment for him, gathering upon him the punishment for the major sins (al-kabā'ir) that he committed.

{And [whoever] believed and did righteous deeds, those — Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds

And His saying: ﴿and he will abide therein in humiliation﴾, meaning: he will abide therein, having been struck with disgrace and abasement. It was read as يُضَاعف and يخلد with a ḍamma (raf') and their raf' is by istinaf (a resumptive new sentence, not dependent on what precedes). It was also read as يُضَاعف and يخلد with a sukūn (jazm), and their jazm is as a response to the conditional (jawāb al-sharṭ).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 70:

His saying: ﴿Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds﴾ means: except for those who feel remorse, believe in their Lord, and do righteous deeds in the future.

And His saying: ﴿For those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri, Mujahid, and a group said: this refers to the worldly life. Its meaning is the replacement of disbelief with faith, of association (shirk) with sincerity (ikhlas), and of disobedience with obedience.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and a group said: this refers to the Hereafter, and Allah, the Exalted, replaces the evil deeds of the penitent with good deeds in his record of deeds (sahifah).

A sound report from the Prophet has come concerning the second opinion, narrated by Waki', from al-A'mash, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dhar, that the Prophet said: "A believer will be brought forward on the Day of Resurrection, and his minor sins will be presented to him, while his major sins will be concealed from him. He will be questioned and will confess, and he will be fearful of the major sins. Then Allah, the Exalted, will say: 'Give him a good deed in place of every evil deed.' He will say: 'O Lord, I have sins that I do not see here.' Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed until his molar teeth became visible." Related by Muslim in his Sahih.

And from Abu Hurayrah that he said: The believer will be given his record on the Day of Resurrection, and he will read part of it, and behold, it contains evil deeds. When he reaches the good deeds, he will look briefly at what came before them, and behold, all of them have become good deeds.

A group of the earlier scholars denied that an evil deed can be transformed into a good deed, among them al-Hasan al-Basri and others. But when the report from the Prophet is established, no one has any further word to say.

Some of them have said: Allah erases all evil deeds through remorse, and then establishes a good deed in place of each evil deed.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 71:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous deeds﴾. Some of the scholars (ahl al-'ilm) said: This refers to repentance from other than what has been mentioned before. As for the repentance mentioned in the first verse, it is from the major sins (kaba'ir) that were mentioned before.

Some of them said: This verse also concerns repentance from all bad deeds (sayyi'at), and its meaning is in two respects. The first: the meaning of the verse is, "Whoever intends repentance and resolves upon it, let him repent seeking the Face of Allah the Exalted, and he should not intend anything else." This is like a man saying: "Whoever engages in trade, let him trade in what is righteous, and whoever debates, let him debate in matters of jurisprudence (fiqh)." So His saying ﴿for indeed he turns to Allah in a (sincere) turning﴾ is, according to this view, a statement in the sense of a command, meaning: "Repent to Allah with a (sincere) repentance." The second respect: the meaning of the verse is, "Whoever repents, let him know that his repentance is to Allah, his return is to Him, and his reward is from Him." This is like a man saying to another: "When you speak to the commander (amir), know that he is the commander, and when you speak to your father, know that he is your father."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 72:

His saying: ﴿And those who do not witness false hood﴾ means: the shirk (association of partners with God). Its meaning is: they do not bear witness to the testimony of shirk. It is also said: it means lying. And it is narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya that it means singing (al-ghina'), and this is the view of Mujahid.

(And from some of them): singing is the incantation of fornication. And some of the early scholars (ahl al-salaf) said: singing produces hypocrisy (nifaq) in the heart. It is also said: "they do not witness false hood" means the festivals of the disbelievers. It is also said: it means wailing (al-nawh).

His saying: ﴿And when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity﴾ means: they pass by turning away, as noble people pass by. It is also said: they honour themselves by not entering into it. Al-Hasan said: idle talk (al-laghw) is all sins.

Amr ibn Qays said: it is the gathering of obscenity (al-khana). And laghw in the language is everything that is false and does not benefit anything.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 73:

The Most High said: ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the signs of their Lord, do not fall upon them deaf and blind.﴾

Al-Qutaybi (Ibn Qutaybah) said: its meaning is that they do not heedlessly pass over them, as if they were deaf and did not hear them, and as if they were blind and did not see them. Some others said: its meaning is that they do not fall upon them deaf and blind; rather, they hear and they see.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 74:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and our offspring comfort of the eyes, and make us leaders for the righteous."﴾ That is: children who are dutiful and pious. "Qurrat al-'ayn" (comfort of the eye) is mentioned at times of joy, and "sukhnat al-'ayn" (heat of the eye) at times of sorrow. It is said: the tears of the eye at times of joy are cool, and at times of sorrow they are hot. Abu Mansur al-Azhari mentioned that the meaning of "qurrat al-'ayn" is that one's heart finds what it is pleased with, so that the eye is at rest from looking at anything else; that is, it does not look at anything else.

It is related from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: Nothing is more comforting to the eye of the believer than to see his family and his offspring pious and dutiful.

And His saying: ﴿And make us leaders for the righteous.﴾ Al-Hasan said: we follow the righteous, and the righteous follow us.

Some scholars have used this verse as evidence that there is no harm in seeking leadership in religion, and that it is recommended.

Others said: one should not seek leadership for worldly authority, but one should seek it for the sake of religion; then the righteous will follow him, and he will become a leader for them, as Allah, may He be exalted, has said.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 75:

His words: ﴿Those will be rewarded with the high chamber (al-ghurfa) for what they endured patiently﴾. ʿAṭāʾ related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "The ghurfa is of pearl, chrysolite and ruby." It is also said: "It is the highest of the dwellings of Paradise."

His words: ﴿for what they endured patiently﴾: that is, patient over the desires (al-shahawāt). It was also said: they were patient regarding the world (al-dunyā). And it was said: they were patient in obedience (al-ṭāʿa).

His words: ﴿and they will be met therein﴾. It was recited as "wa-yulaqqawn" (with a light, unstressed doubled letter), and the meaning is one and the same.

His words: ﴿with a greeting (taḥiyya)﴾. That is, a kingship (mulk). It was also said: enduring life (baqāʾ) [always].

His words: ﴿and peace (salāman)﴾. That is, they greet one another with peace. ʿAṭāʾ related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "Allah greets them with peace." It was also said: safety from calamities.

Allah's words: ﴿Abiding therein; excellent is it as a place of rest and a station﴾. That is, a place where they settle.

And His words: ﴿and a station﴾, that is, they dwell in a lasting dwelling.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 25, verse 77:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: "My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication."﴾ The best of the opinions regarding it is that its meaning is: "What would My Lord do with you were it not for your supplication?" That is, were it not for His calling you to monotheism (al-tawhid). This is similar in meaning to the words of the Exalted: ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?﴾

Al-Qutaybi said: its meaning is: "My Lord would not care for your punishment were it not for your faith," meaning: if you believe, He will not punish you. Some others said: that is, "You would have no worth with your Lord were it not that He called you to faith, so that you would believe; now your worth and standing become manifest to you."

As for His words: ﴿For you have denied,﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas recited: "For the disbelievers have denied." The well-known reading is ﴿For you have denied,﴾ meaning: "You, O disbelievers, have denied." Its meaning is: "I have called you to faith, but you did not believe."

As for His words: ﴿So it will be a binding punishment (lizam).﴾ This is a threat; its meaning is: "The punishment will certainly be binding (lazim)." Ibn Masʿud said: the meaning of al-lizam is the Day of Badr. Some others said: al-lizam is death.

The poet said:

(He turned away at our time of need, a companion, and I did not fear the binding death.)

And it was recited in an irregular reading (shadhdh) as "lazaman" with a fatḥah on the lam, and it has the same meaning as the first.
